# Model Families

`timm` has 1356 architectures in 98 model families, with 1812 pretrained weights. Each family page lists the papers,
architectures and pretrained weights of a model module, and which parts of the [Model API](model_api) its models
support. See the [Quickstart](quickstart) for loading and using the models, the [models reference](reference/models) for
`create_model` and the pretrained configs, and the [results](results) for the ImageNet validation results of all
weights.

## Convolutional networks

* [Aligned Xception](models/xception-aligned) (5 architectures, 6 weights): Aligned Xception (41, 65, 71 layers) as
  modified in DeepLab, implemented from scratch and compatible with the TensorFlow DeepLab weights.
* [BYOBNet (GENet, RepVGG, MobileOne, ...)](models/byobnet) (53 architectures, 57 weights): Bring-Your-Own-Blocks
  Network, a flexible network built from dataclass configs that stack blocks into stages. It implements GPU-Efficient
  Networks (`gernet_*`), RepVGG, MobileOne, RegNetZ, the ResNet image towers of CLIP (`*_clip`) and a number of ResNet
  style `timm` variants.
* [ConvMixer](models/convmixer) (3 architectures, 3 weights): ConvMixer embeds the image as patches and keeps that
  resolution throughout, alternating depthwise convolutions (spatial mixing) and pointwise convolutions (channel
  mixing).
* [ConvNeXt](models/convnext) (31 architectures, 101 weights): ConvNeXt is a pure convolutional network that adopts
  design choices from vision transformers, such as large depthwise kernels, inverted bottlenecks and LayerNorm.
  ConvNeXt-V2 adds Global Response Normalization (GRN) and is pretrained as a fully convolutional masked autoencoder
  (FCMAE).
* [CSPNet (CSPResNet, CSPDarkNet, DarkNet)](models/cspnet) (23 architectures, 15 weights): Cross Stage Partial Networks
  split the features of each stage into two parts, one passing through the stage blocks and one merged back at the end
  of the stage. This module holds CSPResNet, CSPResNeXt, CSPDarkNet, DarkNet and the `timm` `cs3*` variants.
* [CSPNeXt](models/cspnext) (5 architectures, 5 weights): The CSPNeXt backbone of the RTMDet real-time object detector
  (CSP blocks with 5x5 depthwise convolutions), with ImageNet-1k classification weights converted from the OpenMMLab
  checkpoints.
* [DenseNet](models/densenet) (6 architectures, 6 weights): Densely connected convolutional networks, where each layer
  in a dense block takes the concatenated outputs of all preceding layers of the block. Adapted from torchvision,
  `densenetblur` uses blur pool anti-aliased downsampling.
* [DLA](models/dla) (12 architectures, 12 weights): Deep Layer Aggregation (DLA) networks merge features across blocks
  and stages with iterative and hierarchical aggregation nodes. Includes DLA variants built from Res2Net blocks.
* [DPN](models/dpn) (7 architectures, 7 weights): Dual Path Networks combine a residual path (feature re-use) and a
  densely connected path (new feature exploration) in each block. Compatible with the weights of the original MXNet
  implementation.
* [HRNet](models/hrnet) (11 architectures, 14 weights): High-Resolution Networks keep a high resolution branch through
  the whole network and add lower resolution branches in parallel, repeatedly exchanging information between them.
* [Inception-ResNet-v2](models/inception-resnet-v2) (1 architecture, 2 weights): Inception-ResNet-v2 combines Inception
  modules with residual connections. Ported from the TensorFlow implementation and weights.
* [Inception-v3](models/inception-v3) (1 architecture, 4 weights): Inception-v3, adapted from the torchvision
  `Inception3` model.
* [Inception-v4](models/inception-v4) (1 architecture, 1 weight): Inception-v4, ported from the TensorFlow
  implementation and weights.
* [InceptionNeXt](models/inception-next) (4 architectures, 5 weights): InceptionNeXt decomposes the large kernel
  depthwise convolution of ConvNeXt into parallel branches, a small square kernel, two orthogonal band kernels and an
  identity mapping, following Inception.
* [MambaOut](models/mambaout) (11 architectures, 12 weights): MambaOut stacks Gated CNN blocks, Mamba blocks without the
  state space model (SSM) token mixer, to test whether SSMs are needed for image classification.
* [NASNet](models/nasnet) (1 architecture, 1 weight): NASNet-A Large, a network of cells found by neural architecture
  search, from Cadene's pretrained models port.
* [NFNet](models/nfnet) (36 architectures, 14 weights): Normalization-Free networks, trained without batch normalization
  using scaled weight standardization: NFNet (with adaptive gradient clipping), NF-RegNet and pre-activation NF-ResNet
  models.
* [PNASNet](models/pnasnet) (1 architecture, 1 weight): PNASNet-5 Large, found by progressive neural architecture
  search, from Cadene's pretrained models port.
* [PP-HGNet](models/hgnet) (10 architectures, 19 weights): PP-HGNet and PP-HGNetV2 (High Performance GPU Net) from
  PaddleClas, built from HG blocks that aggregate the outputs of a sequence of convolutions. The `ssld` weights are
  trained with PaddleClas SSLD distillation.
* [RDNet](models/rdnet) (4 architectures, 5 weights): RDNet (DenseNets Reloaded) revisits densely connected
  convolutional networks with modernized blocks and design choices.
* [RegNet](models/regnet) (36 architectures, 65 weights): RegNetX and RegNetY networks from the regular network design
  spaces, RegNetZ from "Fast and Accurate Model Scaling", and `timm` additions such as the pre-activation RegNetV.
  Includes weights from pycls, torchvision and VISSL (SEER).
* [Res2Net](models/res2net) (9 architectures, 9 weights): Res2Net splits the channels of the bottleneck block into
  groups connected hierarchically, giving several receptive field sizes within one block. Includes Res2NeXt.
* [ResNeSt](models/resnest) (8 architectures, 8 weights): ResNeSt uses split-attention blocks, channel attention across
  groups of feature map splits, in a ResNet style network.
* [ResNet](models/resnet) (81 architectures, 149 weights): Residual networks (ResNet) and the variants built on the same
  `ResNet` class: ResNeXt grouped convolutions, Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) and ECA channel attention, deep / tiered
  stems and average pool downsampling (the "c", "d", "s" and "t" variants), anti-aliased downsampling, Wide ResNet and
  ResNet-RS configurations.
* [ResNetV2 (BiT)](models/resnetv2) (20 architectures, 24 weights): Pre-activation ResNet (v2) with Group Normalization
  and Weight Standardization as used by Big Transfer (BiT), with the original BiT weights. Also supports the non
  pre-activation variant used as the hybrid Vision Transformer backbone.
* [SelecSLS](models/selecsls) (5 architectures, 3 weights): SelecSLS uses selective long and short range skip
  connections, proposed as the core network of XNect, a real-time multi-person 3D pose estimation system.
* [SENet (legacy)](models/senet) (9 architectures, 9 weights): SENet, SE-ResNet and SE-ResNeXt from Cadene's pretrained
  models (`legacy_*`). The module is deprecated in favour of the SE variants of the `ResNet` class.
* [SKNet](models/sknet) (5 architectures, 3 weights): Selective Kernel Networks on a ResNet base, where SK units fuse
  branches with different kernel sizes using attention over the branches.
* [TResNet](models/tresnet) (4 architectures, 10 weights): TResNet is a ResNet based design for high GPU throughput,
  with a space-to-depth stem, anti-aliased downsampling and SE layers.
* [VGG](models/vgg) (8 architectures, 8 weights): VGG networks of stacked 3x3 convolutions, adapted from torchvision
  with `timm` functionality added.
* [VoVNet](models/vovnet) (10 architectures, 3 weights): VoVNet uses One-Shot Aggregation (OSA) modules, which
  concatenate the outputs of all layers of a block once at its end. VoVNetV2 (from CenterMask) adds residual connections
  and effective SE (eSE) attention.
* [Xception (legacy)](models/xception) (1 architecture, 1 weight): The original Xception, depthwise separable
  convolutions with residual connections, with weights ported from Keras (`legacy_xception`).

## Vision Transformers

* [BEiT](models/beit) (7 architectures, 13 weights): BEiT and BEiT-v2 Vision Transformers, pretrained with masked image
  modeling. BEiT predicts the discrete visual tokens of masked patches, BEiT-v2 uses a vector-quantized visual tokenizer
  for the targets. The weights here are fine-tuned classification weights.
* [CaiT](models/cait) (10 architectures, 10 weights): Class-Attention in Image Transformers (CaiT), deep Vision
  Transformers that use LayerScale and finish with class-attention layers, which update only the class token from the
  patch tokens.
* [ConViT](models/convit) (3 architectures, 3 weights): ConViT replaces the self-attention of the early Vision
  Transformer blocks with gated positional self-attention (GPSA), which can be initialized to behave like a convolution,
  as a soft convolutional inductive bias.
* [CrossViT](models/crossvit) (11 architectures, 11 weights): CrossViT processes small and large image patches in two
  Transformer branches and fuses them with cross-attention through the class tokens. Model names in `timm` give the
  actual input resolution (240 / 408 instead of the original 224 / 384).
* [DaViT](models/davit) (8 architectures, 5 weights): Dual Attention Vision Transformers (DaViT) combine spatial window
  attention and channel group attention, both linear in the number of tokens, in a hierarchical design.
* [DeiT](models/deit) (16 architectures, 24 weights): Data-efficient Image Transformers (DeiT) are Vision Transformers
  trained on ImageNet-1k only, optionally with a distillation token that learns from a CNN teacher. DeiT III models are
  trained with an improved recipe.
* [EVA](models/eva) (65 architectures, 83 weights): EVA and EVA-02 Vision Transformers and other ViT variants sharing
  the `Eva` class, with rotary position embeddings (RoPE), SwiGLU MLPs and related additions. The module also holds the
  Perception Encoder (PE), ROPE-ViT, DINOv3, LingBot-Vision and Sapiens2 models and `timm` original ViT configs with
  RoPE.
* [GCViT](models/gcvit) (5 architectures, 5 weights): Global Context Vision Transformers (GCViT) alternate local window
  attention with global context attention, whose queries are generated from the whole feature map by a convolutional
  module.
* [Hiera](models/hiera) (8 architectures, 16 weights): Hiera is a hierarchical vision transformer without specialized
  modules (convolutions, shifted windows, relative position biases), relying on masked autoencoder (MAE) pretraining to
  learn spatial biases.
* [HieraDet (SAM 2)](models/hieradet-sam2) (5 architectures, 8 weights): HieraDet, the Hiera based image encoder of
  Segment Anything 2 (SAM 2), with windowed attention and windowed position embeddings.
* [MViTv2](models/mvitv2) (8 architectures, 7 weights): Multiscale Vision Transformers v2, a hierarchical transformer
  with pooling attention, decomposed relative position embeddings and residual pooling connections.
* [NaFlex ViT](models/naflexvit) (8 architectures, 5 weights): A Vision Transformer with the patch embedding and
  position encoding in one module, supporting pre-patchified inputs with variable aspect ratio and resolution (NaFlex),
  FlexiViT variable patch size and NaViT factorized position embeddings.
* [NesT](models/nest) (6 architectures, 3 weights): Nested Transformers (NesT) apply self-attention locally within
  non-overlapping image blocks and aggregate neighbouring blocks between stages. Weights converted from the official JAX
  release.
* [PiT](models/pit) (8 architectures, 8 weights): Pooling-based Vision Transformers (PiT) reduce the spatial size and
  increase the channels of the tokens between stages with a depthwise convolution pooling layer, as in CNNs.
* [PVTv2](models/pvt-v2) (7 architectures, 7 weights): Pyramid Vision Transformer v2, a hierarchical transformer with
  spatial-reduction attention (linear in the `_li` variant), overlapping patch embeddings and convolutional feed-forward
  layers.
* [Segment Anything ViT](models/vision-transformer-sam) (4 architectures, 3 weights): The ViT image encoder of the
  Segment Anything Model (SAM), a plain ViT backbone with windowed and global attention blocks and relative position
  embeddings as in ViTDet.
* [Swin Transformer](models/swin-transformer) (9 architectures, 19 weights): Swin Transformer is a hierarchical vision
  transformer that computes self-attention within local windows, shifted between consecutive blocks for cross-window
  connections. Includes the S3 (AutoFormerV2) weights.
* [Swin Transformer V2](models/swin-transformer-v2) (12 architectures, 12 weights): Swin Transformer V2 scales up Swin
  with residual post-norm, scaled cosine attention and a log-spaced continuous relative position bias that transfers
  across window sizes.
* [Swin Transformer V2 (CR)](models/swin-transformer-v2-cr) (16 architectures, 3 weights): An alternative Swin
  Transformer V2 implementation adapted from Christoph Reich's code, designed for changing the image size together with
  the window size, including non-square sizes. The module docstring marks it as experimental.
* [TNT](models/tnt) (3 architectures, 3 weights): Transformer in Transformer (TNT) models the structure inside each
  patch with an inner transformer over sub-patches, alongside the outer transformer over patches.
* [Twins](models/twins) (6 architectures, 6 weights): Twins-PCPVT (Pyramid Vision Transformer with conditional position
  encodings) and Twins-SVT (spatially separable self-attention, locally grouped attention alternating with global
  sub-sampled attention).
* [Vision Transformer (relative position)](models/vision-transformer-relpos) (13 architectures, 9 weights): Vision
  Transformers using relative position biases instead of absolute position embeddings. The module docstring marks these
  models as experimental.
* [Vision Transformer (ViT)](models/vision-transformer) (157 architectures, 302 weights): The Vision Transformer (ViT)
  splits an image into fixed size patches, linearly embeds them and processes the resulting token sequence with a
  standard Transformer encoder. This module holds the `VisionTransformer` class and the weights for the original ViT,
  the "How to train your ViT?" (AugReg) and FlexiViT models, and many image-text (CLIP, SigLIP) and self-supervised
  pretrained image towers that share the architecture.
* [VOLO](models/volo) (11 architectures, 11 weights): Vision Outlooker (VOLO) adds outlook attention, which encodes
  fine-level features from local neighbourhoods, before transformer stages that operate on coarser tokens.
* [XCiT](models/xcit) (28 architectures, 42 weights): Cross-Covariance Image Transformers (XCiT) replace token
  self-attention with cross-covariance attention across feature channels, linear in the number of tokens, and add local
  patch interaction layers.

## Hybrid convolution / attention networks

* [BYOANet (BoTNet, HaloNet, LambdaNet)](models/byoanet) (15 architectures, 13 weights): Networks built with the
  `ByobNet` block / stage config system that place self-attention (or similar) layers in ResNet style stages: Bottleneck
  Transformers (BoTNet), HaloNets and Lambda ResNets. The module docstring marks these definitions as experimental.
* [CoaT](models/coat) (8 architectures, 8 weights): Co-Scale Conv-Attentional Image Transformers (CoaT) use factorized
  attention with convolution based relative position encodings, and a co-scale mechanism that exchanges information
  between parallel blocks at different scales.
* [CSATv2](models/csatv2) (2 architectures, 3 weights): CSATv2 is a frequency-domain vision model that works on DCT
  transforms of the input image, with spatial attention.
* [FocalNet](models/focalnet) (12 architectures, 12 weights): Focal Modulation Networks (FocalNet) replace
  self-attention with focal modulation, which aggregates context at several granularities with depthwise convolutions
  and gates it into each query token.
* [Hybrid Vision Transformer](models/vision-transformer-hybrid) (14 architectures, 14 weights): Vision Transformers
  whose patch tokens come from a convolutional backbone (ResNet / ResNetV2 stem or stages) instead of a linear patch
  embedding, using the `VisionTransformer` class.
* [LeViT](models/levit) (20 architectures, 10 weights): LeViT is a hybrid network for fast inference, a convolutional
  stem followed by attention stages that shrink the resolution with attention based downsampling and use attention
  biases for position.
* [MaxViT and CoAtNet](models/maxxvit) (56 architectures, 52 weights): From-scratch implementations of MaxViT (MBConv
  blocks with multi-axis attention, blocked local and dilated grid attention) and CoAtNet (convolution stages followed
  by relative attention stages), plus `timm` variants (`_rw` configs, MaxxViT).
* [MetaFormer (PoolFormer, ConvFormer, CAFormer)](models/metaformer) (18 architectures, 50 weights): MetaFormer models
  share a general transformer block structure and vary the token mixer: pooling in PoolFormer / PoolFormerV2, separable
  convolutions in ConvFormer, and convolutions in the early stages with attention in the later stages in CAFormer.
* [Next-ViT](models/nextvit) (3 architectures, 12 weights): Next-ViT is a hybrid CNN / transformer for efficient
  deployment, stacking Next Convolution Blocks (NCB) and Next Transformer Blocks (NTB).
* [TinyViT](models/tiny-vit) (5 architectures, 11 weights): TinyViT is a family of small hierarchical vision
  transformers (a convolutional first stage, then local window attention), pretrained by fast distillation from large
  teacher models.
* [Visformer](models/visformer) (2 architectures, 2 weights): Visformer (Vision-friendly Transformer) transitions a
  transformer towards a convolutional design, with convolutional blocks in the early stage and self-attention in the
  later stages.
* [ViTamin](models/vitamin) (13 architectures, 15 weights): ViTamin is a vision model designed for vision-language
  models, with convolutional (MBConv) stages followed by transformer stages. The weights are CLIP image towers.

## Efficient and mobile networks

* [CPUBone](models/cpubone) (9 architectures, 9 weights): CPUBone is a vision backbone designed for devices with low
  parallelization capabilities, such as CPUs, built from (fused) MBConv blocks and convolutional attention blocks.
* [EdgeNeXt](models/edgenext) (5 architectures, 6 weights): EdgeNeXt is a hybrid CNN-Transformer for mobile devices that
  combines depthwise convolution encoders with split depth-wise transpose attention (SDTA) encoders, which apply
  attention across channels.
* [EfficientFormer](models/efficientformer) (3 architectures, 3 weights): EfficientFormer is a vision transformer
  designed for mobile latency, with pooling based blocks on 4D feature maps in the early stages and multi-head
  self-attention blocks in the last stage.
* [EfficientFormer-V2](models/efficientformer-v2) (4 architectures, 4 weights): EfficientFormer-V2 revisits the
  EfficientFormer design to reduce both parameter count and latency for mobile devices, with convolutional stages and
  attention in the later, lower resolution stages.
* [EfficientNet](models/efficientnet) (115 architectures, 119 weights): EfficientNet and EfficientNetV2, and the related
  mobile architectures built from the same depthwise separable, inverted residual (MBConv) and fused MBConv blocks:
  MixNet, MnasNet, FBNet, Single-Path NAS, MobileNet-V1 / V2, EfficientNet-Lite, EdgeTPU and TinyNet.
* [EfficientViM](models/efficientvim) (8 architectures, 12 weights): Efficient Vision Mamba (EfficientViM) is built
  around the Hidden State Mixer based State Space Duality (HSM-SSD) layer, implemented here in plain PyTorch. The
  `_dist` models add a distillation head.
* [EfficientViT (MIT)](models/efficientvit-mit) (7 architectures, 19 weights): EfficientViT from the MIT Han Lab, a
  vision backbone for high-resolution, low-computation recognition that uses multi-scale linear attention.
* [EfficientViT (MSRA)](models/efficientvit-msra) (6 architectures, 6 weights): EfficientViT from Microsoft Research, a
  memory efficient vision transformer with cascaded group attention, which feeds each attention head a different split
  of the features.
* [FasterNet](models/fasternet) (6 architectures, 6 weights): FasterNet is built around partial convolution (PConv),
  which convolves only a part of the input channels to reduce redundant computation and memory access.
* [FastViT](models/fastvit) (12 architectures, 21 weights): FastViT is a hybrid convolutional / transformer network that
  uses structural reparameterization to remove skip connections at inference. The module also includes the MobileCLIP
  image encoders (`fastvit_mci*`).
* [GhostNet](models/ghostnet) (10 architectures, 5 weights): GhostNet generates part of its feature maps with cheap
  operations (Ghost modules). GhostNetV2 adds DFC attention for long-range dependencies, GhostNetV3 uses
  re-parameterization and knowledge distillation in training.
* [HardCoRe-NAS](models/hardcorenas) (6 architectures, 6 weights): Mobile networks found by HardCoRe-NAS, a
  differentiable neural architecture search with hard latency constraints, built on the `MobileNetV3` class.
* [iFormer](models/iformer) (9 architectures, 8 weights): iFormer integrates a fast convolutional network with
  single-head modulation attention (SHMA) in the later stages, for mobile applications.
* [LowFormer](models/lowformer) (8 architectures, 7 weights): LowFormer is a convolutional transformer backbone designed
  for hardware efficiency (measured throughput and latency rather than MACs). The E1 / E2 / E3 edge GPU variants are
  from the journal extension.
* [MobileNet-V3](models/mobilenetv3) (33 architectures, 45 weights): MobileNet-V3 and the related networks built on the
  same `MobileNetV3` class: MobileNet-V4, LCNet (PP-LCNet), FBNet-V3 and TensorFlow ported MobileNet-V3 weights
  (`tf_*`).
* [MobileViT](models/mobilevit) (10 architectures, 16 weights): MobileViT combines MobileNet-V2 inverted residual blocks
  with MobileViT blocks, which apply transformers to unfolded patches for global processing. MobileViT-V2 uses separable
  self-attention. Built on the `ByobNet` class.
* [PP-LCNetV2](models/lcnetv2) (3 architectures, 4 weights): PP-LCNetV2 from PaddleClas is a CPU oriented network built
  on PP-LCNet. The depthwise convolutions of the later stages are re-parameterizable multi-scale branches, and SE and
  shortcuts are used sparingly to avoid latency penalties on CPU.
* [RepGhost](models/repghost) (8 architectures, 8 weights): RepGhostNet replaces the feature concatenation of the Ghost
  module with re-parameterized feature reuse, folded into a single convolution path at inference.
* [RepViT](models/repvit) (8 architectures, 13 weights): RepViT is a mobile CNN that brings design choices of
  lightweight vision transformers into MobileNet-V3 style blocks, with structural re-parameterization.
* [ReXNet](models/rexnet) (10 architectures, 9 weights): ReXNet revises the channel configuration of inverted residual
  networks to reduce representational bottlenecks. The `rexnetr_*` variants round the channels to multiples of 8.
* [SHViT](models/shvit) (4 architectures, 4 weights): SHViT (Single-Head Vision Transformer) uses a memory efficient
  macro design and single-head attention applied to part of the channels.
* [StarNet](models/starnet) (7 architectures, 4 weights): StarNet is a deliberately simple proof-of-concept network
  built around the star operation, the element-wise multiplication of two branches.
* [SwiftFormer](models/swiftformer) (4 architectures, 4 weights): SwiftFormer replaces the quadratic matrix
  multiplications of self-attention with efficient additive attention, for real-time mobile vision applications.

## MLP and other token mixers

* [MLP-Mixer, ResMLP and gMLP](models/mlp-mixer) (15 architectures, 19 weights): All-MLP architectures that alternate
  token mixing across patches with channel mixing: MLP-Mixer, ResMLP and gMLP (gating with a spatial projection). The
  module docstring notes the gMLP implementation is not verified.
* [Sequencer](models/sequencer) (3 architectures, 3 weights): Sequencer replaces self-attention with BiLSTM layers that
  mix tokens along the vertical and horizontal axes, followed by channel MLPs.

## Multimodal model vision encoders

* [DeepSeek ViT](models/deepseek-vit) (3 architectures, 6 weights): The vision encoder of the DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1
  multimodal models, a pre-norm ViT with RMSNorm, a SwiGLU MLP and axial 2D RoPE as the only position encoding.
  Classifier variants add pooling and a linear head, the `_enc` variants keep the native projector that maps the tokens
  to the language model width.
* [Gemma 4 ViT](models/gemma4-vit) (4 architectures, 4 weights): The vision encoder of Google's Gemma 4 multimodal
  models, a ViT with 2D RoPE, gated MLPs, QK normalization and sandwich normalization blocks.
* [MobileNet-V5](models/mobilenetv5) (3 architectures, 1 weight): The MobileNet-V5 vision encoder from Google's Gemma
  3n, built from MobileNet-V4 blocks (Universal Inverted Residual, Mobile MQA) with a multi-scale fusion adapter.
* [Qwen3 ViT](models/qwen3-vit) (9 architectures, 39 weights): The vision encoder of the Qwen3-VL / Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8
  multimodal models, a pre-norm ViT with a learned absolute position grid combined with axial 2D RoPE. Classifier
  variants add pooling and a linear head, the `_enc` variants keep the native projector that maps the tokens to the
  language model width.
